title: Add AWS Route 53 to Micetro

cta.text: See Micetro with your own AWS account

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Add AWS Route 53 to Micetro".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Add AWS Route 53 to Micetro" and whose text is exactly: Watch BlueCat Micetro connect an AWS account, then show its Route 53 zones and VPC networks beside Azure and your on-premises servers, and write a new record to Route 53.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
6 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. One set of AWS credentials connects the account: a name for the service, an access key ID and its secret, with DNS and IPAM both on. New in 26.2, you can cap how fast Micetro calls AWS, here at five requests per second. Review the settings, then select Add.
2. The service is added. Micetro now reads the AWS account on its own, and the new row sits in the list with Azure and your on-premises servers.
3. The account's eleven Route 53 zones are now in Micetro, public and private, with AWS as the authority. They sit in the same list as every other zone. Pick one to see its records.
4. A zone lists its records in the same view as on any other platform. Select Create to add one.
5. Select Save and the record is written to Route 53 in your AWS account. portal now sits in the zone, and AWS holds the same record.
6. IPAM has the account's networks too. Its 18 VPCs show under their own AWS account, across 17 regions, beside the Azure account and your on-premises ranges. AWS DNS is managed in Micetro the same way as the rest of your estate.
